LESSON: READING FOR COMMUNICATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Reading 2.6 Skimming for information (2 Lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, 
Topic 2.7: Reading for Communication

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading for Communication. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can reading enhance knowledge?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify language structures in reading comprehension

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify language structures in reading comprehension
   In simple words: practise until you can identify language structures in reading comprehension. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading for Communication using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading for Communication in the examples.
2. Explain Reading for Communication to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading for Communication.
4. Show that you can: identify language structures in reading comprehension

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading for Communication using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading for Communication important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Search (from different sources) and read out with peers what kind of illnesses their peers suffer from,
2. Listen to and read along a text about people talking about being ill (z.B. Ich bin krank; ich habe Kopfweh/Kopfschmerzen; Ich gehe zum Ärzt; Ich gehe ins Krankenhaus; usw), and carry out given tasks
3. Look at a diagram and read the designated body parts while speculating about what could be hurting (z.B. Sein Kopf tut ihm weh; Er hat Rückenschmerzen; usw),
4. Read a poster listing symptoms of various illnesses,

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify language structures in reading comprehension

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
